Of Health.     Of Ecology.      Of Fairness.          Of Care.
Organic agriculture combines
tradition, innovation and science to
benefit the shared environment and
promotes fair relationships and a
good quality of life for all involved.
INTRODUCTION                                 DEFINITION OF ORGANIC
                                             AGRICULTURE
The terms of reference for these
principles1 are based on the SAOSO           The PGS operates within the principles
Standard for Organic Production and          and guidelines of IFOAM�Organics
Processing. The SAOSO Standard               International and therefore adopts as
describes organic agriculture as a           its definition of organic agriculture:
whole system approach based upon
a set of processes resulting in a            "Organic agriculture is a
sustainable ecosystem, safe food, good       production system that
nutrition, animal welfare and social         sustains the health of soils,
justice. Therefore, organic production       ecosystems and people. It
is more than a system of production          relies on ecological processes,
that includes or excludes certain inputs.    biodiversity and cycles adapted
The SAOSO Standard is written in such        to local conditions, rather than
a way that producers wishing to follow       the use of inputs with adverse
the Standard may use it in the context       effects. Organic agriculture
of third party certification, Participatory  combines tradition, innovation
Guarantee Systems (PGS), Community           and science to benefit the
Supported Agriculture (CSA), or simply       shared environment and
self-commitment.                             promotes fair relationships
                                             and a good quality of life for
The Standard describes specifics             all involved."
allowed and restricted inputs, various
technical specifications and notifiable
exceptions. The principles below are
in harmony with these standards, and
should not be seen as a substitute, but
rather as a complimentary framework;
written in language that all participants
can understand, in the positive
spirit of participation and integrity �
cornerstones of any PGS.

 1. Ecosystem Management                  as described in the SAOSO Organic
                                          Standard. The wild harvest areas

                                          any contamination, whether it be
                                          agrochemical or industrial pollutants.

                                          2. Soil Management

                                          Organic agriculture starts with the soil.
                                          It is a basic principle that plant health
                                          is a reflection of soil health. The farm
                                          must have a clear long term soil fertility
                                          management system in place. This
                                          system should include the following:
